Stack.description: Flex container. direction: "row"|"column" (default "column"). gap: "none"|"xs"|"s"|"m"|"l"|"xl"|"2xl" (default "m"). align: "start"|"center"|"end"|"stretch"|"baseline". justify: "start"|"center"|"end"|"between"|"around"|"evenly".

TextContent.description: Text block. Supports markdown. Optional size: "small" | "default" | "large" | "small-heavy" | "large-heavy".

MarkDownRenderer.description: Renders markdown text with optional container variant ("clear" | "card" | "sunk"). Use for long-form documents, README content, or markdown with code blocks. For short UI text and labels, use TextContent.

TextCallout.description: Standalone callout for important context or guidance. Use only inside Stack or Card

Tag.description: Compact semantic tag or badge with optional icon token

TagBlock.description: tags is an array of strings

Image.description: Image that supports url, base64, or inline SVG

Card.description: Styled container. variant: "card" (default, elevated) | "sunk" (recessed) | "clear" (transparent). Always full width. Accepts all Stack flex params (default: direction "column"). Cards flex to share space in row/wrap layouts.

CardHeader.description: Header with optional title and subtitle

Descriptions.description: Descriptions-style detail view for a single record with optional bordered and plain visual modes. DescField ONLY lives inside Descriptions.

DescField.description: Declarative descriptions field with label, direct value expression, and optional span. Must be used inside Descriptions; when orphaned, auto-renders as a single-field Descriptions.

Form.description: Form container with fields and explicit action buttons

DatePicker.description: Date picker supporting single and range selection

Modal.description: Modal dialog. open is a reactive $boolean binding — set to true to open, X/Escape/backdrop auto-closes. Put Form with buttons inside children.

CheckBoxGroup.description: CheckboxGroup component with items and CheckboxGroup wraps each item

CheckBoxItem.description: Checkbox item with label and optional description

RadioGroup.description: Radio group for selecting one option from a list

RadioItem.description: Standalone radio toggle with optional label and description

SwitchItem.description: Standalone switch toggle with optional label and description

Slider.description: Numeric slider input; supports continuous and discrete variants

FormControl.description: Field with name, input component, label text and optional hint text

Col.description: Declarative table column. Use Col(title, field, options?) instead of writing a raw columns JSON object.

IndexCol.description: Row-number column for Table. IndexCol("序号") — title is required.

Table.description: Data table: Table(columns, rows, expandRow?). Col(title, field, options?) defines each column. IndexCol(title) adds a row-number column. ExpandRow (3rd arg) renders expandable content per row — use @Render("row", ...)

PieChart.description: Circular slices; use for protocol distribution or traffic breakdown by source

LineChart.description: Lines over time; use for latency, throughput, or any time-series metric

BarChart.description: Vertical bars; use for comparing values across categories or devices

HorizontalBarChart.description: Horizontal bars; use for long category labels, ranked lists, or interface throughput comparison

AreaChart.description: Filled area under lines; use for bandwidth utilization, cumulative traffic, or capacity trends

RadarChart.description: Radar/spider chart; use for comparing multiple metrics across devices or interfaces

ScatterChart.description: Scatter points; use for correlations like latency vs packet loss or throughput vs error rate. Pass xType='time' when X values are epoch millisecond timestamps to enable automatic date axis formatting.

Series.description: A named data series for multi-series charts. values[i] pairs with chart's labels[i], so values.length MUST equal labels.length.

ScatterSeries.description: A named scatter series with data points for ScatterChart

Point.description: A data point with optional z dimension for bubble charts

TabItem.description: value is unique id, trigger is tab label, content is array of components

Steps.description: Ordered step-by-step procedure. Every item must be a StepsItem.

StepsItem.description: One step with optional expandable details. Details may contain text, components, or nested StepsItem values.

componentGroups.name: Layout
notes: - For grid-like layouts, use Stack with direction "row" and wrap=true. Avoid justify="between" unless you specifically want large gutters.
- Use nested Stacks when you need explicit rows/sections.
- Use Tabs for alternative views (chart types, data sections) instead of inventing ternary show/hide patterns.
- For nested data, prefer Tabs + @Each when outer items represent a small set of groups/views and the nested content is the main content.

componentGroups.name: Content
notes: - Use MarkDownRenderer for long-form text with code blocks; use TextContent for short UI labels.
- Use Cards to group related KPIs or sections. Stack with direction "row" for side-by-side layouts.
- Wrap charts in a Card with CardHeader for titled sections.

componentGroups.name: Tables
notes: - Cell renderer: `Col(title, field, {cell: @Render("v", expr)})` — `v` is the cell value.

- When the renderer needs other row fields, declare the second binder: `@Render("v", "row", expr)`. Keep all logic that combines `v` and `row` inside that single template — do not reference `row` unless you declared it.
- Do not add a chart that simply re-pairs record names with one numeric field from a Table. Use charts when the data is chart-ready or a trend/distribution is the user's request.
- For nested arrays, use Table expandRow when there are too many outer items for Tabs.
- When a Table field is a string array, render it with `TagBlock` instead of displaying the raw array or joining it into plain text.

componentGroups.name: Descriptions
notes: - Prefer Descriptions for single-record detail views; reserve Table for arrays of records.
- DescField ONLY lives inside Descriptions — never use DescField as a direct child of Card, Stack, or any other component.
- To show multiple field groups, use separate Descriptions calls side-by-side: Descriptions([field1, field2], "Group A", null, 2) + Descriptions([field3, field4], "Group B", null, 2).
- When Descriptions will contain 6+ fields, set `columns=2` to avoid crowding (long device names, ports, IPs need horizontal space).
- The `format` prop on `DescField` was removed. Wrap values with `@FormatX(...)` directly.

componentGroups.name: Charts (2D)
notes: - Only use chart components when the data model exposes chart-ready fields matching the signature. For raw row records, prefer Table or Descriptions.

- For positional tuple arrays like `[timestamp, value]`, project the index first: `@Each(data.samples, "item", @FormatDate(item[0], "dateTime"))` for labels, `@Each(data.samples, "item", item[1])` for values.

- When a multi-series LineChart is built by partitioning a flat array (e.g. `@Filter` over an entity field), derive the labels axis from one of the partitioned slices, NOT the unpartitioned source — the unpartitioned array has length N × entityCount while each filtered series has only N values, which leaves the right side blank.
- If per-entity timestamps do not align across slices, use ScatterChart with Point pairs (or one LineChart per entity) so each series carries its own X axis.
- Do not invent labels, series, categories, or missing time points just to make a chart render.

componentGroups.name: Charts (1D)
notes: - PieChart takes parallel labels[] and values[] arrays of NUMBERS (not objects): PieChart(["Low", "Med", "High"], [12, 28, 7], "donut").

componentGroups.name: Charts (Scatter)
notes: - When X values are epoch millisecond timestamps, pass `xType='time'` (4th arg) so the X axis is formatted as dates instead of raw numbers.

componentGroups.name: Forms
notes: - For Form fields, define EACH FormControl as its own reference — do NOT inline all controls in one array. This allows progressive field-by-field streaming.
- NEVER nest Form inside Form — each Form should be a standalone container.
- Form requires explicit buttons. Always pass a Buttons(...) reference as the second Form argument: Form(name, buttons, fields).
- rules is an optional object: {required: true, email: true, minLength: 8, maxLength: 100}
- Available rules: required, email, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, url, numeric
- The renderer shows error messages automatically — do NOT generate error text in the UI

componentGroups.name: Data Display
notes: - For boolean fields (active, enabled, status), use a ternary: `v ? Tag("Active", "success") : Tag("Inactive", "danger")`. `@Switch` matches string keys so `{true: ...}` won't match boolean values.

examples:
root = Stack([kpiRow, tableCard])
kpiRow = Stack([countKpi, avgKpi, activeKpi], "row", "m", "stretch", "start", true)
countKpi = Card([TextContent("Total Employees", "small"), TextContent("" + @Count(data.employees), "large-heavy")])
avgKpi = Card([TextContent("Avg Salary", "small"), TextContent("" + @FormatNumber(@Avg(data.employees.salary), 1), "large-heavy")])
activeKpi = Card([TextContent("Active", "small"), TextContent("" + @Count(@Filter(data.employees, "active", "==", 1)), "large-heavy")])
tableCard = Card([tableHeader, employeeTable])
tableHeader = CardHeader("Employee Directory", "Salary, status and 7-day trend")
employeeTable = Table([nameCol, salaryCol, joinedCol, statusCol, perfCol], data.employees)
nameCol = Col("Name", "name", {cell: @Render("v", "row", Link("http://localhost:5173/" + row.id, v))})
salaryCol = Col("Salary", "salary", {cell: @Render("v", TextContent(@FormatNumber(v, 1)))})
joinedCol = Col("Joined", "joinedAt", {cell: @Render("v", TextContent(@FormatDate(v, "date")))})
statusCol = Col("Status", "active", {cell: @Render("v", @Switch(v, {"1": Tag("Active", "success"), "0": Tag("Inactive", "danger")}, Tag("Unknown")))})
perfCol = Col("Performance", "perfRatio", {cell: @Render("v", TextContent(@FormatPercent(v, 1)))})
skillsCol = Col("Skills", "skills", {cell: @Render("v", @Count(v) > 0 ? TagBlock(v) : TextContent("No data"))})

root = Stack([kpiCard])
kpiCard = Card([kpiHeader, kpiChart])
kpiHeader = CardHeader("Latency Trend", "Hourly samples, last 6 hours")
timestampLabels = @Each(data.samples, "item", @FormatDate(item[0], "dateTime"))
sampleValues = @Each(data.samples, "item", item[1])
kpiChart = LineChart(timestampLabels, [Series("Latency", sampleValues)], "smooth", "Time", "ms")

root = Stack([trendCard])
trendCard = Card([trendHeader, trendChart])
trendHeader = CardHeader("Group Comparison", "Value trend by group")
groupASlice = @Filter(data.records, "groupKey", "==", "group-a")
groupBSlice = @Filter(data.records, "groupKey", "==", "group-b")
trendLabels = @FormatDate(groupASlice.timestamp, "dateTime")
groupASeries = Series("Group A", groupASlice.value)
groupBSeries = Series("Group B", groupBSlice.value)
trendChart = LineChart(trendLabels, [groupASeries, groupBSeries], "smooth", "Time", "Value")

root = Stack([detail])
detail = Descriptions([DescField("Name", data.user.name ?? "No data"), DescField("Region", data.user.region ?? "No data")], "Profile")

root = Stack([reportHeader, dimCards])
reportHeader = CardHeader("网络健康报告", "综合健康分: " + data.healthScore)
dimCards = Stack(@Each(data.data, "dim", dimTpl))
dimTpl = Card([CardHeader(dim.key, "得分: " + dim.value.rootValue + " · 排名: " + dim.value.rank), LineChart(@Each(dim.value.baseline, "b", @FormatDate(b.timestamp, "date")), [Series("Baseline", dim.value.baseline.value), Series("Essential", dim.value.essential.value)], "smooth", "时间", "数值"), Stack([Table([Col("区域", "regionName"), Col("数值", "value"), Col("层级", "level")], dim.value.rankList), Table([Col("子指标", "key"), Col("数值", "value")], dim.value.subValues)], "row", "m")])

# Nested Array Example
root = Stack([summaryCard, modelTabs])
modelTabs = Tabs(@Each(data.grouped_by_model, "group", modelTabTpl))
modelTabTpl = TabItem(group.model, group.model + " (" + group.count + ")",[table])
table = Table([Col("Device Name", "name"), Col("IP", "ip"), Col("Version", "version"), Col("Vendor", "vendor")], group.devices)
additionalRules: JS globals do not exist: String(), Number(), Date(), Math.*, JSON.* are parse errors. `+` auto-converts: write `"Total: " + data.count`, never `String(...)`.
Functions do not exist: `(d) => ...` and `function` are parse errors. Repeat concrete definitions per instance (cardA = Card(...), cardB = Card(...)), or use @Each/@Render.
Use openui-lang concatenation with `+` for display strings; do not use JavaScript conversion helpers.

Never hardcode data values from the data model — always reference fields via data paths or derived variables. Accessing a field on an array extracts that field from every element: `filteredRows.fieldName` returns an array of values, useful for building Series.

When host data is provided, never invent, backfill, or synthesize labels, rows, metrics, statuses, timestamps, percentages, or records that are absent. For null-dominant records, preserve real non-null fields and show missing ones with `?? "No data"` (or `"Unknown"`, `"?"`, or omit).

For field names containing spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII text (e.g. Chinese field names), ALWAYS use bracket notation: `data.peer_interface_info["本端接口"]` — never use dot notation like `data.peer_interface_info.本端接口`.

builtins.description: Sort array by field. Direction: "asc" (default) or "desc"

builtins.signature: Filter(array, field, operator: "==" | "!=" | ">" | "<" | ">=" | "<=" | "contains", value) -> filtered array

builtins.description: Convert a plain object map into ordered rows of {key, value}. Returns [] for null, arrays, and unsupported inputs.
Return the ordered keys of a plain object map. Returns [] for null, arrays, and unsupported inputs.
Map an enum value to a display result via a cases object. Numeric values are coerced to strings for key lookup. Returns default (null if omitted) when no case matches.

Format a date-like value for display. `value` accepts a Unix timestamp in seconds OR milliseconds (auto-detected), an ISO 8601 string; also maps over arrays. `style` accepts "date", "dateTime", "time", or "relative", defaults to "date".
Format a byte count into a compact SI string (KB, MB, GB). Returns "" for nullish input.
Format a scalar number as a locale-aware display string. Returns raw input for invalid values.
Format a ratio (e.g. 0.125) as a locale-aware percentage string that already includes the % symbol (e.g. "12.5%"). Do NOT append + "%" to the result.
Format an elapsed duration into a compact display string. Input defaults to seconds and also supports explicit "ms" input.
Evaluate template for each element. varName is the loop variable - use it ONLY inside the template expression (inline). Do NOT create a separate statement for the template.
Create a deferred render template for prop values. Binder names are string literals and are only in scope inside the template body.
